A novel approach to the problem of unsupervised feature learning is presented.

1) we propose an unsupervised framework to adapt a generic pedestrian detection network to a new multisensory target domain, 2) we propose a novel TS-RPN architecture to learn the multisensory features from both thermal and visible images for robust pedestrian recognition, and 3) we present an auto labeling framework to iteratively predict pedestrian instances in visible thermal channels and merge them for generating multispectral annotations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing an unsupervised framework to learn the multispectrum features from the raw data without any manual annotation effort.
